newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: FERNANDEZ ATTACKS ARGENTINE ALLIANCE ON CURRENCY.
newsitem.headline: FERNANDEZ ATTACKS ARGENTINE ALLIANCE ON CURRENCY.

text.p: Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez tried to cast doubt Thursday on the commitment to peso parity of the new opposition alliance that is posing a serious challenge to the ruling Peronist Party.

The former Central Bank chief, who usually stays outside the political fray, dismissed as "pure electoral opportunism" the new Radical Party/Frepaso alliance for October's mid-term elections in Congress and the 1999 presidential race.

Fernandez, speaking to reporters at a banking conference, questioned the center-left alliance leaders' public promises to respect the Convertibility Law that has maintained the peso at par to the dollar since 1991.
Convertibility is credited with eliminating inflation and bringing Argentina unaccustomed economic stability.

Some Radical Party leaders, including ex-President Raul Alfonsin, had previously criticized Convertibility and other free-market reforms by Peronist President Carlos Menem, but now say they support them.
"Unless the alliance justifies why it voted against the structural reforms, I will have serious doubts about their real commitment to Convertibility," said the minister.
